So I'm going to make sure that I talk about that and the fact that no longer is -- are checkups invasive, necessarily. segments.speaker: Rebecca Johns
segments.text: Good morning. Rebecca Johns, Legal Department. I am here to make a presentation upon your request about our Bay area Legal Services program that we have. We started this program in 2022 to help city residents who were having landlord tenant issues. This includes issues with condition of the property or the landlord breaching the contract or eviction. The way the program is set up is city residents call the housing hotline, and then the city, if they meet the requirements for the types of cases, the city will refer those cases to bay area. Bay area then screens them and make sure they meet income requirements and other requirements that the bay area has. In 2022, the city funded up to $75,000. Bay area ended up only expending 2900 of that. There were nine referrals over and bay area handled two cases. In 2023, the city funded again $75,000. Bay area expended 6900. Eight referrals and bay area handled five cases. 2024, city funded again 75,000. Bay area expended 5900. Five referrals and bay area handled three cases. In 2025, the city funded up to $10,000. Bay area actually expended zero. There were two cases, but they build them to a different funding source, so none of the money was taken out of the city funding. A lot of the calls that we get from residents are for rental assistance. Because that's not a legal issue, those cases don't get referred to bay area. So we've been working with bay area to figure out how to better serve more residents. So what we've come up with is a lot of the residents are calling bay area directly, and they are not coming through our hotline. The way the contract is set up right now, we would not fund those cases because they didn't come through the hotline. We are bringing a new contract back to you where residents can directly contact bay area and bay area can draw down on city funding for that. Bay area believes they have enough of the volume that that will take up the city funding.

segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Green. Ashley followed by Mr. Doss. My name is ashley morrow. I want to thank the City Council for the opportunity to serve on the Charter Review Commission. What I am is someone who enjoys advocating for people who may not always have a voice or a seat at the table. To the people out here who are apathetic, you lose democracy when people stop participating, which is why it was shocking to me to know that Tampa did not have an inspector general. A noninterference provision calls out, obviously, using some of the language that was provided to us. We added in language that the office may utilize the services of the Human Resources Department but not be subject to its authority because there was some discussion about being overridden by executive. We also included language that the council had asked for regarding the various officers not being able to direct this individual or impede them. Council indicated that you'd like to have an implementing ordinance for some of the details here. We did include some basic provisions using the miami beach model that was recommended to us, along with others, that some minimum standards to say what this ordinance has to include, which includes having this inspector general selection committee, the membership, procedures, process for appointment and reappointments, that this be an open merit-based process. Also the ordinance would set the number of personnel for the office, provide for initial funding because obviously there would not be a budget at the time this was established and provide the employees of the office be entitled to the same benefits as similarly situated employees. This is language that also appears in your city clerk provision. So we were mirroring that. To be clear, since this section sits outside of both the legislative branch and the executive branch, we included a provision that this office doesn't exercise powers of the other branches. It has access to the individuals but does not usurp their powers. It does though grant them specific powers in the next section as far as initiating an investigation, audit or review or acting on its own initiative. We gave the office the discretion to decide whether or not they wish to proceed if something is in the public interest or not. And also that they had the power to file ethics complaints, refer matters outside, independent, obviously, of the rest of the city. For subpoena authority, given the desire to include that, we looked again to the miami beach model, and they had some interesting language there that we thought was useful about making sure that they could seek judicial enforcement of subpoenas. But we also had some caveats that they had to inquire whether there was a companion criminal investigation going on as to not interfere with that. It was a very interesting provision. Sub-2 that talks to the fact they can't use subpoenas to battle somebody else with subpoena authority over them. Again, trying to prevent a vicious circle.
